goldens.comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.

With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows UsernameForm.java at line 47 calling `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. Looking at the diff, the only `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` method defined is in UsernamePasswordForm.java with signature `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` requiring a UserModel parameter. UsernameForm extends AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator (not UsernamePasswordForm), so it would not inherit this method. The zero-argument version does not exist in the diff, meaning this would be a compilation error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernamePasswordForm.java:161 — `return webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null;` now prevents WebAuthn form setup whenever the user is initially unknown, so normal passwordless/passkey login no longer renders or submits conditional UI (severity P1, confidence 99%).

adjudication.rationale: The finding misreads the code. The method `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` at line 161 returns true when `user != null`, but this is used in the `authenticate()` and `challenge()` methods to determine when to call `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)`. Looking at the diff, the original code at lines 113-116 only called `fillContextForm` when `context.getUser() == null` (inside the else branch). The new code at lines 118-120 calls it when `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` returns true, which requires `user != null`. This is actually a change in behavior, but the finding claims it 'prevents WebAuthn form setup whenever the user is initially unknown' - however, the original code DID set up WebAuthn when user was null (inside the else block). The new logic requires user to be non-null. But examining the full context, the `authenticate()` method structure shows the WebAuthn setup was moved outside the if-else block, and the condition changed. The finding's claim about 'normal passwordless/passkey login' is incorrect because passkeys with conditional UI work differently - they're triggered by the browser's autocomplete, not by server-side form setup. The `fillContextForm` is for showing authenticator options, not for conditional UI.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/webauthn/passwordless/PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:294 — P2 (90% confidence): `catch (Exception nsee)` treats any Selenium/runtime failure while locating the WebAuthn form as the expected absence, so the test can pass without actually proving that passkeys are hidden (the same masking occurs at line 315).

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the test code at lines 294 and 315 uses a broad `catch (Exception nsee)` block to verify that the WebAuthn form is absent. Looking at the diff, the test expects `driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']"))` to throw an exception when passkeys are not available, but catching all Exceptions (not just NoSuchElementException) could mask other failures. However, this is a test quality concern rather than a bug - the test logic is intentional (checking element absence), just implemented with overly broad exception handling. This is a valid code review concern about test robustness, not a functional defect.
